title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund Bill 2018
short_title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill creates a new financial fund to help the Commonwealth pay the Indigenous Land Corporation.
Money and assets from the existing Land Account would go into the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund, run by the Future Fund Board.
The explanatory memorandum does not give the start date for the fund or the exact amount to be transferred.
changes: Establishes the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund as a dedicated financial asset.
Transfers monies and assets from the Land Account to the new fund.
Has the Future Fund Board manage the fund to generate investment returns.
summary.affected: The Commonwealth, the Indigenous Land Corporation, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

speeches.speaker: Ken Wyatt
speeches.brief: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund Bill 2018 establishes a new investment fund managed by the Future Fund Board of Guardians to ensure sustainable, long-term funding for the Indigenous Land Corporation, following nationwide consultations where a majority of stakeholders supported replacing the restricted low-return investment mandate of the existing Land Account.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Labor supported the bill to expand the Indigenous Land Corporation’s functions to include water-related rights, renaming it the Indigenous Land and Sea Corporation, following consultations where over 75% of sessions supported the reforms.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Amendment (Indigenous Land Corporation) Bill 2018, which expands the ILC's functions to include acquisition and management of water-related rights for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. He also noted that a social justice package promised alongside the land fund was never implemented.

speeches.speaker: Linda Burney
speeches.brief: Labor will support the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund Bill 2018 in the House. The bill contains six schedules.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund Bill, noting the ILC board retains oversight of the account and welcoming the requirement for the Future Fund to brief the board on investments. They argued for establishing a national representative body for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, citing the loss of ATSIC and inadequate funding for the National Congress of Australia's First Peoples.

speeches.speaker: Ken Wyatt
speeches.brief: The bill closes the $2 billion Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land Account and establishes a new Future Fund managed by the Future Fund Board of Guardians to invest in a broader range of products, aiming to ensure sustainable funding for the Indigenous Land Corporation. Annual payments to the Corporation will remain indexed at over $53 million, while additional payments will be reformed to support the fund's long-term sustainability.

speeches.speaker: Ken Wyatt
speeches.brief: The speaker moved four government amendments to the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2018, replacing references to the "Indigenous Land Corporation Board" with "Indigenous Land and Sea Corporation Board" to align with separate renaming legislation. The amendments and bill were commended to the House to enable the effective operation of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Land and Sea Future Fund.
